title: introduce horizon-aware batch merger to reduce padding and KV-cache churn
author: Maya Chen
body:
Context and motivation: Batching by simple seqlen buckets reduces padding but leaves two important costs unaddressed: (1) KV-cache churn across requests with similar prefixes but divergent remaining horizons, and (2) kernel selection thrashing when small numbers of long and short sequences are combined. This PR introduces a horizon-aware batch merger (HABM) scheduler that greedily merges queued requests taking into account predicted remaining horizon, kernel compatibility, and an estimated padding+cost objective. The goal is to reduce per-token compute cost and KV-cache misses while preserving latency SLOs for short queries.

Design summary: HABM computes a horizon_score for each request: horizon_score = alpha * predicted_remaining_tokens + beta * kernel_affinity_score + gamma * recent-prefix-cache-hit-probability. Predicted_remaining_tokens is drawn from a lightweight per-route distribution (histogram/EMA) maintained by the console instrumentation; kernel_affinity_score is a discrete bucket describing which execution kernel (fp16/fp8/quantized path) the request is likely to prefer based on model and temperature; cache-hit-probability is estimated from prefix hash frequency in the last N minutes. The scheduler maintains a sliding merge window (configurable in ms) and performs a fast greedy merge that attempts to maximize a negative-cost function: benefit = estimated_cache_hits * cache_weight - padding_tokens * padding_weight - latency_penalty * P90_delta. If benefit > merge_threshold the batch is emitted to the runtime; otherwise the request is emitted as-is to avoid latency regression.

Implementation notes: 
- New scheduler module: runtime/scheduler/habm_scheduler.cc + header. The implementation is C++ with a minimal dependency footprint and a pluggable policy API so alternate heuristics can be registered.
- Per-route horizon stats: controller/metrics/horizon_histogram_store.go which ships histograms to the control plane and exposes a lightweight REST endpoint for the scheduler to pull hot keys.
- KV-cache affinity tags: runtime/cache/prefix_affinity.*—adds a short-lived affinity token (16-bit) to requests to identify likely cache reuse groups.
- Kernel affinity markers: runtime/kernel/kernel_registry updates to allow kernel-affinity-aware packing (ensures kernel-compatible sequences share CUDA kernel launch).
- Fallbacks: HABM integrates with existing bucketed-batcher; when habitability checks fail (low traffic or high heterogeneity) HABM will delegate to the seqlen-bucketed path.

Testing and benchmarks: 
- Unit tests: scheduler/habm_scheduler_test.cc covers merge decisions under synthetic distributions.
- Integration: end-to-end bench harness under benchmark-lab/bench/habm_mixedlen.sh reproduces mixed workloads (20/50/200 token distributions).
- Microbenchmarks: on p4d.24xlarge we observe a 9-12% throughput increase (tokens/sec) and 6-9% lower per-token GPU time for mixed-length, bursty workloads compared to current seqlen-bucketed baseline. Short-query P50 latency is within 3% of baseline with default thresholds. Detailed results attached in PR artifacts (ci/artifacts/habm-bench-20241114.zip).

Operational considerations: 
- Runtime flags: --habm-window-ms (default 10ms), --habm-cache-weight (default 1.5), --habm-padding-weight (default 1.0). Defaults tuned conservatively to avoid latency regressions.
- Metrics added: habm/merged_batches, habm/predicted_horizon_distribution, habm/cache_reuse_rate, habm/padding_tokens_saved. These appear in the console dashboards after this merge.
- Rollout: feature guarded under runtime.feature_flags.habm; integration tests included to validate disabled->enabled transition.

Related work: this is complementary to the seqlen-bucketing family; HABM focuses on horizon prediction and cache affinity rather than static bucketing. See ENG-5124 for product acceptance criteria and ENG-5281 for benchmark automation.

Security and compatibility: no new network surface. Kernel registry additions are backward-compatible; HABM can be disabled via feature flag per-cluster.

How to exercise locally: 
1) make build && ./bin/redwood-runtime --config ./examples/configs/local.yaml --feature habm=on 
2) ./benchmark-lab/bench/habm_mixedlen.sh --clients 200 --duration 2m 

Notes: I kept the scheduler deterministic for reproducible perf runs and added a small randomized jitter to avoid pathological alignment across racks. The PR intentionally keeps thresholds conservative; further tuning will be driven by Canary results.

Checklist: 
- [x] unit tests added 
- [x] integration bench harness added 
- [x] telemetry and dashboards wired 
- [x] feature-flagged for safe rollout

Merge strategy and outcome: squashed and merged to main after two approvals and a green CI run.
commits: c1a8f3d: introduce habm scheduler + policy interface
f4b2aa1: add horizon histogram store and REST endpoint
7e6c2b9: kernel affinity tagging and cache affinity tokens
d3098ef: tests, docs, bench harness and default config flags
review_comments: Rafael Ortiz: Overall this looks promising. Two asks: expose the merge_threshold as a runtime knob and add an e2e latency regression test focusing on P95 for short queries.

Maya Chen (author): Added merge_threshold runtime flag and added e2e regression test under tests/e2e/habm_latency_regression.py. Test is gated behind ci tag 'perf-e2e' to avoid flakiness on presubmit.
Priya Nair: Please add an explanation in docs/ops/habm.md about when HABM will defer to the bucketed-mode. Also concerned about memory overhead for horizon histograms in high-cardinality routes.
Maya Chen (author): Documentation updated and histograms are capped per-route (configurable cardinality cap, default 100 hot routes). Added a note about memory cap and eviction policy in ops doc.
Samir Gupta: Benchmarks look good, but can we add one more comparison with kv-cache disabled to isolate kernel packing gains?
Maya Chen (author): Added an additional bench run to artifacts and a short section in the PR body summarizing the isolated kernel-packing gain (~3% tokens/sec) when cache is disabled.
Priya Nair: Approving pending CI pass.
release_notes: Introduce horizon-aware batch merger (HABM) scheduler to improve throughput for mixed-length workloads.
Feature-flagged; metrics and dashboards added. Default thresholds conservative to avoid latency regressions.
